summary:
### TL;DR
- Secret scanning now has SpaceX as a partner and a new detector for `starlink_public_api_v2_secret`. Detectors for Alibaba, AWS, Google, OpenVSX, Pydantic Services and Tencent now filter out more false positives. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-05-secret-scanning-upgrades-detectors-adds-spacex-as-partner))
- The Copilot usage metrics API has a new `copilot_code_review` object. It lets you track a per-repository "addressed rate", with breakdowns that include a `security` comment type. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-05-usage-metrics-api-adds-code-review-details-and-addressed-rate))
- None of today's entries are Actions-specific, and there are no breaking changes or deadlines.

### Action required
Nothing this time.

### Security improvements
- **New secret scanning partner and detector:** SpaceX joined the secret scanning partnership program. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-05-secret-scanning-upgrades-detectors-adds-spacex-as-partner))
  - When a `starlink_public_api_v2_secret` is found in a public repository, GitHub forwards it to SpaceX so they can revoke or rotate it.
  - The same secret type is now detected automatically in your repositories.
- **Fewer false positives in secret scanning:** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-05-secret-scanning-upgrades-detectors-adds-spacex-as-partner))
  - **AWS, Alibaba and Google Cloud Storage:** these key ID/secret detectors now suppress unpaired matches when dictionary filtering removes all qualifying companion secrets. The affected AWS types are `aws_access_key_id`, `aws_session_token` and `aws_temporary_access_key_id`.
  - **OpenVSX (`openvsx_access_token`):** tighter context matching, so unrelated UUIDs are not treated as legacy tokens.
  - **Pydantic Logfire (`logfire_token`):** matches the documented token length and character set, which excludes placeholder values and public browser tokens.
  - **Tencent (`tencent_cloud_secret_id`):** requires both letters and digits after the prefix, which excludes alphabetic identifiers such as function names.
  - Expect less alert noise. Note that unpaired AWS, Alibaba and Google key IDs may no longer raise alerts in the filtered cases.
- **Visibility into Copilot code review outcomes:** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-05-usage-metrics-api-adds-code-review-details-and-addressed-rate))
  - **Where it appears:** each row of the enterprise and organization `repos-1-day` reports now includes:
    - `total_comments_evaluated` and `total_comments_addressed`
    - breakdowns by severity, review tier, comment type (including `security`) and customization
    - `total_merged_no_human_change_request_after_review`
  - **Security use:** this can show whether security-related review comments are actually being acted on.
  - **Counting rules:**
    - Comments are counted on the day the pull request merges, not the day they were posted.
    - Comments on bot-opened pull requests are usually not evaluated.
  - **Access:**
    - Requires the Copilot usage metrics policy to be enabled.
    - Available to enterprise owners, enterprise billing managers, organization owners, and custom roles with the View Copilot Metrics permission.

### Docs changes worth reading
No documentation changes in this period.

changelog.title: Usage metrics API adds code review details and addressed rate
changelog.text: The enterprise and organization repository-level Copilot usage metrics reports now show what happens to Copilot code review feedback. A new copilot_code_review object on each repos-1-day row reports how many Copilot-reviewed pull requests merged without a later change request from a person and how many Copilot code review comments developers acted on. With these you can track an addressed rate per repository. What’s new total_comments_evaluated : The number of Copilot code review comments checked to see whether the developer acted on them. total_comments_addressed : The number of evaluated comments the developer acted on, whether by applying the suggestion, asking Copilot to make the fix, editing the code, or replying that the fix will come in a later pull request. Divide by total_comments_evaluated for the addressed rate. review_comments_by_severity , review_comments_by_review_tier , review_comments_by_comment_type , and review_comments_by_customization : Both counts broken down by severity (e.g., high , medium , low ), review tier (e.g., lite , balanced , max ), comment type (e.g., bug , security , or custom for your repository’s own coding guidelines), and customization (e.g., custom instructions, skills, MCP servers, or none). total_merged_no_human_change_request_after_review : The number of merged pull requests that Copilot code review reviewed where no person requested changes after Copilot’s first review. Why this matters The existing pull_requests fields show how often Copilot code review runs and how often someone clicks to apply a suggestion, but developers act on most feedback in other ways. These fields show whether developers act on Copilot code review feedback in each repository, which kinds of comments land, whether custom instructions, skills, and MCP servers make a difference, and whether reviewers still request changes after Copilot reviews. Important notes Scope: Present on every row of the enterprise and organization repos-1-day reports. Counts are 0 and arrays are empty when a repository had no Copilot code review activity that day. Counted on merge: Comments are evaluated when their pull request merges, so they count on the merge day, not the day Copilot posted them. Bot pull requests: Copilot usually doesn’t evaluate comments on pull requests opened by bots, such as Copilot cloud agent. total_merged_no_human_change_request_after_review still includes those pull requests. Different from suggestion counts: pull_requests.total_copilot_applied_suggestions counts only ready-to-apply suggestions that someone applied. The new counts include every evaluated comment and count them as addressed however the developer acted on them. Access: Enterprise owners, enterprise billing managers, organization owners, and anyone with a custom organization or enterprise role that grants the View Copilot Metrics permission can access these reports. The Copilot usage metrics policy must be enabled. Visit the Copilot usage metrics API documentation to get started. The post Usage metrics API adds code review details and addressed rate appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Secret scanning upgrades detectors, adds SpaceX as partner
changelog.text: This update expands secret scanning’s detection coverage: New partner: SpaceX is now a secret scanning partner. New detector: GitHub now detects starlink_public_api_v2_secret . Upgraded detectors: Alibaba, AWS, Google, OpenVSX, Pydantic Services, and Tencent detectors include additional false-positive filtering. New secret scanning partners The following provider joined the secret scanning partnership program. When one of their secrets is found in a public repository, GitHub forwards it to the partner so they can revoke or rotate the credential before it can be abused. Provider Secret type SpaceX starlink_public_api_v2_secret Detectors added Secret scanning now automatically detects the following new secret type in your repositories. Provider Secret type SpaceX starlink_public_api_v2_secret Partner secrets are automatically reported to the secret issuer when found in public repositories through the secret scanning partnership program . User secrets generate secret scanning alerts when found in public or private repositories. False positives reduced The following detector improvements reduce false-positive matches for supported secrets. Provider Secret type Improvement Alibaba alibaba_cloud_access_key_id Suppress unpaired matches when dictionary filtering removes all qualifying companion secrets. AWS aws_access_key_id Suppress unpaired matches when dictionary filtering removes all qualifying companion secrets. AWS aws_session_token Suppress unpaired matches when dictionary filtering removes all qualifying companion secrets. AWS aws_temporary_access_key_id Suppress unpaired matches when dictionary filtering removes all qualifying companion secrets. Google google_cloud_storage_access_key_secret Suppress unpaired matches when dictionary filtering removes all qualifying companion key identifiers. Google google_cloud_storage_service_account_access_key_id Suppress unpaired matches when dictionary filtering removes all qualifying companion secrets. Google google_cloud_storage_user_access_key_id Suppress unpaired matches when dictionary filtering removes all qualifying companion secrets. OpenVSX openvsx_access_token Tighten context matching for legacy tokens to avoid treating unrelated UUIDs as credentials. Pydantic Services Inc. logfire_token Match the documented token length and character set to exclude placeholder values and public browser tokens. Tencent tencent_cloud_secret_id Require both letters and digits after the token prefix to exclude alphabetic identifiers such as function names. Learn more Learn more about secret scanning and see the full list of supported secrets in our documentation. Let us know what you think in the community discussion .
